request: Add an `is_valid_email` function to lnbits/helpers.py and use it to validate email in account updates.

summary.result_text:
I couldn't run the tests because the permission prompt for `make test-unit` wasn't approved, so none of this has been verified.

- **Existing code:** `lnbits/helpers.py` had no email validator. Four other files already import `is_valid_email_address` from it (`core/models/users.py`, `core/views/auth_api.py`, `core/services/notifications.py`, `tests/unit/test_helpers.py`), so those imports would fail.
- **Email check:** I added `is_valid_email(email)` to `lnbits/helpers.py`. It rejects addresses over 254 characters and requires a local part, `@`, and a domain with a dot and a TLD of at least two letters. So `alice@example` is invalid, as `tests/unit/test_helpers.py` expects.
- **Alias:** I kept `is_valid_email_address = is_valid_email` in `lnbits/helpers.py`, so the four existing imports resolve without edits. Say so if you'd rather I rename them to `is_valid_email` and drop the alias.
- **Account updates:** `Account.validate_fields()` in `lnbits/core/models/users.py` now calls `is_valid_email`. `update_user_account` runs `validate_fields()` first, so both the admin `PUT /user/{id}` route and the user's own account updates validate the email.

I didn't add new tests, since `tests/unit/test_helpers.py` already covers the valid and invalid cases.

Please run `make test-unit` to confirm. I'd also run `make check` for lint and type checks.

input.command: git status --short && git log --oneline -3 && grep -rn "email_address" lnbits/helpers.py; grep -n "email" -B3 -A12 tests/unit/test_helpers.py | sed -n 1,60p; grep -n "update_user_account" -r lnbits | head
